chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: The Turf and a blind church pianist friend
summary: Talk of the Turf and a piano-playing neighbor who played in church, with whom he played trombone.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Didn't you also hang out at a place called the Turf?
That's where I met Billie Holiday. Don't you remember me telling you?
This girl that you ( ? ) on Prospect Avenue ( ? ) You came to my house. on ( ? ) Avenue.
This was a lady, and you went to play with her, to have a jam session.
Hazel Scott or Mary Lou Williams?
No, I never played with - ... Wait, I'll get this chick straight here.
No, we don't forget it. I mean, it's tough to remember all these things... Didn't she live in your building?

May have been. She lived under you. That's right, now I got you covered. I forgot her name, 'cause I used to take my horn and go in and play with her, sure did. She died; you told me she died, didn't she? ... Yes you did, you certainly did. I'll never forget it.
What was so significant about that? What was the important thing about this?
Nothing... Just like a lady that lived down on the next floor - she's blind but she can play anything you want to, anything.

She played in church. Name is Mamie, that's all I know. I don't care what tune you played, the only thing she'd say is, what key, and play. They are very dear friends of ours, especially the lady that Margaret lived with, Minnie - you know Minnie. Minnie, that lived on the next floor? We played for a birthday party down there, and she played too. I think she played in a church practically every Sunday...

The way you're speaking about this friend here, did many of your friends, musician friends, get together in a friendship atmosphere like that, when you didn't get together just to play with each other but just to talk. To jive with each other -
Nothing but piano and trombone, that was all.
